title_en: Cryptography Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: This Law is formulated in order to regulate the application and administration of cryptography, promote the development of the cryptography industry, ensure network and information security, safeguard national security and public interests, and protect the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations.

For the purposes of this Law, "cryptography" means the technologies, products, and services that use specific transformation methods to perform encryption protection and security authentication on information, etc.

Cryptography work shall adhere to a holistic approach to national security, and follow the principles of unified leadership and graded responsibility, innovative development and service to the overall situation, administration according to law and security assurance.

The leadership of the Communist Party of China over cryptography work shall be upheld. The central cryptography work leading body shall exercise unified leadership over national cryptography work, formulate major policies for national cryptography work, coordinate and consolidate major matters and important tasks of national cryptography, and promote the construction of the rule of law in national cryptography.

The national cryptography administrative department shall be responsible for administering cryptography work nationwide. The cryptography administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for administering cryptography work within their respective administrative regions.
State organs and units involved in cryptography work shall, within their respective functions and duties, be responsible for the cryptography work of their own organs, units, or systems.

The State shall implement classified management of cryptography.
Cryptography is divided into core cryptography, ordinary cryptography, and commercial cryptography.

Core cryptography and ordinary cryptography shall be used to protect information classified as State secrets; the highest classification level of information protected by core cryptography is top secret, and the highest classification level of information protected by ordinary cryptography is secret.
Core cryptography and ordinary cryptography belong to State secrets. The cryptography administrative departments shall, in accordance with this Law and relevant laws, administrative regulations, and relevant State provisions, implement strict and unified management of core cryptography and ordinary cryptography.

Commercial cryptography shall be used to protect information that does not belong to State secrets.
Citizens, legal persons, and other organizations may use commercial cryptography according to law to protect network and information security.

The State encourages and supports research and application of cryptography science and technology, protects intellectual property rights in the field of cryptography according to law, and promotes progress and innovation in cryptography science and technology.
The State strengthens the cultivation of cryptography talents and team building, and commends and rewards organizations and individuals that have made outstanding contributions to cryptography work in accordance with relevant State provisions.

The State shall strengthen cryptography security education in various forms, incorporate cryptography security education into the national education system and the civil servant education and training system, and enhance the cryptography security awareness of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations.

People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate cryptography work into their national economic and social development plans, and include the necessary funds in their fiscal budgets at the corresponding level.

No organization or individual may steal the encrypted information of others or illegally intrude into the cryptography assurance system of others.
No organization or individual may use cryptography to engage in illegal or criminal activities that endanger national security, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others.

The State shall strengthen the scientific planning, management, and use of core cryptography and ordinary cryptography, enhance institutional development, improve management measures, and strengthen the capability for cryptography security assurance.

State secret information transmitted in wired or wireless communications, as well as information systems storing and processing State secret information, shall, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and relevant State provisions, use core cryptography or ordinary cryptography for encryption protection and security authentication.

Organizations engaged in scientific research, production, service, testing, equipment, use, and destruction of core cryptography and ordinary cryptography (hereinafter collectively referred to as cryptography work organizations) shall, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, relevant State provisions, and the requirements of core cryptography and ordinary cryptography standards, establish and improve security management systems, adopt strict confidentiality measures and confidentiality responsibility systems, and ensure the security of core cryptography and ordinary cryptography.

The cryptography administrative departments shall, according to law, provide guidance, supervision, and inspection of the core cryptography and ordinary cryptography work of cryptography work organizations, and the cryptography work organizations shall cooperate.

The cryptography administrative departments shall, based on work needs and together with relevant departments, establish collaboration mechanisms such as security monitoring and early warning, security risk assessment, information notification, consultation on major matters, and emergency response for core cryptography and ordinary cryptography, to ensure the coordinated and orderly and efficient security management of core cryptography and ordinary cryptography.
When cryptography work organizations discover disclosure of core cryptography or ordinary cryptography, or major problems or risks affecting the security of core cryptography or ordinary cryptography, they shall immediately take countermeasures and promptly report to the confidentiality administrative department and the cryptography administrative department, and the confidentiality administrative department and the cryptography administrative department shall, together with relevant departments, organize investigation and handling, and guide the relevant cryptography work organizations to eliminate security risks in a timely manner.

The State shall strengthen the construction of cryptography work organizations to ensure their performance of work duties.
The State shall establish a management system for personnel recruitment, selection and transfer, confidentiality, assessment, training, treatment, rewards and punishments, exchange, and withdrawal that meets the needs of core cryptography and ordinary cryptography work.

The cryptography administrative departments may, due to work needs and in accordance with relevant State provisions, request the public security, transportation, customs, and other departments to provide convenience such as exemption from inspection for articles and personnel related to core cryptography and ordinary cryptography, and the relevant departments shall provide assistance.

The cryptography administrative departments and cryptography work organizations shall establish and improve strict supervision and security review systems, supervise their staff's compliance with laws and discipline, and take necessary measures according to law to organize security reviews regularly or irregularly.

Article 21 The State encourages the research and development, academic exchange, transformation of achievements, and promotion and application of commercial cryptography technologies, and shall improve a unified, open, competitive, and orderly market system for commercial cryptography, and encourage and promote the development of the commercial cryptography industry.
People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall follow the principle of non-discrimination, and treat equally according to law units including foreign-invested enterprises engaged in commercial cryptography research, production, sales, service, import and export, etc. (hereinafter collectively referred to as commercial cryptography practitioners). The State encourages commercial cryptography technical cooperation based on the principle of voluntariness and commercial rules in the process of foreign investment. Administrative agencies and their staff shall not use administrative means to force the transfer of commercial cryptography technologies.
The research, production, sales, service, import and export of commercial cryptography shall not harm national security, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others.

Article 22 The State shall establish and improve the commercial cryptography standards system.
The administrative department for standardization under the State Council and the national cryptography administrative department shall, in accordance with their respective duties, organize the formulation of national standards and industry standards for commercial cryptography.
The State supports social organizations and enterprises in using independent innovation technologies to formulate commercial cryptography group standards and enterprise standards that are higher than the relevant technical requirements of national standards and industry standards.

Article 23 The State promotes participation in international standardization activities for commercial cryptography, participates in the formulation of international standards for commercial cryptography, and advances the transformation and application between Chinese standards and foreign standards for commercial cryptography.
The State encourages enterprises, social organizations, and educational and research institutions, etc., to participate in international standardization activities for commercial cryptography.

Article 24 Commercial cryptography practitioners conducting commercial cryptography activities shall comply with the relevant laws, administrative regulations, compulsory national standards for commercial cryptography, and the technical requirements of the public standards of such practitioners.
The State encourages commercial cryptography practitioners to adopt recommended national standards and industry standards for commercial cryptography, to enhance the protection capability of commercial cryptography, and to safeguard the lawful rights and interests of users.

Article 25 The State promotes the construction of a commercial cryptography testing and certification system, formulates technical specifications and rules for commercial cryptography testing and certification, and encourages commercial cryptography practitioners to voluntarily undergo commercial cryptography testing and certification to enhance market competitiveness.
Commercial cryptography testing and certification institutions shall obtain relevant qualifications according to law, and shall conduct commercial cryptography testing and certification in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations and the technical specifications and rules for commercial cryptography testing and certification.
Commercial cryptography testing and certification institutions shall bear confidentiality obligations for the state secrets and trade secrets that they come to know during commercial cryptography testing and certification.

Article 26 Commercial cryptography products involving national security, the national economy and people's livelihood, or public interests shall be included in the catalogue of critical network equipment and specialized network security products according to law, and may be sold or provided only after they have passed testing and certification by qualified institutions. The testing and certification of commercial cryptography products shall apply the relevant provisions of the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China to avoid duplicate testing and certification.
Where commercial cryptography services use critical network equipment and specialized network security products, they shall be certified as qualified by a commercial cryptography certification institution for such commercial cryptography services.

Article 27 For critical information infrastructure that is required by laws, administrative regulations, and relevant state provisions to be protected using commercial cryptography, its operators shall use commercial cryptography for protection, and shall conduct commercial cryptography application security assessment by themselves or by entrusting a commercial cryptography testing institution. The commercial cryptography application security assessment shall be aligned with the critical information infrastructure security testing and assessment and the network security grade assessment system to avoid duplicate assessment and testing.
Where an operator of critical information infrastructure procures network products and services involving commercial cryptography that may affect national security, it shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China, pass the national security review organized by the national cyberspace administration department jointly with the national cryptography administrative department and other relevant departments.

Article 28 The competent department of commerce under the State Council and the national cryptography administrative department shall, according to law, implement import licensing for commercial cryptography that involves national security, public interests and has encryption protection functions, and implement export controls for commercial cryptography that involves national security, public interests or China's international obligations. The import licensing list and export control list for commercial cryptography shall be formulated and published by the competent department of commerce under the State Council jointly with the national cryptography administrative department and the General Administration of Customs.
Commercial cryptography used in mass consumer products shall not be subject to the import licensing and export control system.

Article 29 The national cryptography administrative department shall recognize institutions that use commercial cryptography technologies to engage in electronic certification services for e-government, and shall jointly with relevant departments be responsible for the management of the use of electronic signatures and data messages in government affairs.

Article 30 Trade associations and other organizations in the commercial cryptography field shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws, administrative regulations and their charters, provide information, technology, training and other services to commercial cryptography practitioners, guide and urge commercial cryptography practitioners to conduct commercial cryptography activities according to law, strengthen industry self-discipline, promote industry integrity building, and facilitate the healthy development of the industry.

Article 31 The cryptography administrative department and relevant departments shall establish a commercial cryptography mid- and post-event supervision system combining routine supervision and random inspections, establish a unified information platform for commercial cryptography supervision and management, promote the linkage between mid- and post-event supervision and the social credit system, and strengthen the self-discipline of commercial cryptography practitioners and social supervision.
The cryptography administrative department and relevant departments and their staff shall not require commercial cryptography practitioners and commercial cryptography testing and certification institutions to disclose proprietary information related to cryptography such as source codes, and shall strictly keep confidential the trade secrets and personal privacy that they know in the performance of their duties, and shall not disclose or illegally provide them to others.

Article 32 Whoever, in violation of Article 12 of this Law, steals the encrypted information of others, illegally invades the cryptographic protection system of others, or uses cryptography to engage in illegal activities that harm national security, public interests, or the lawful rights and interests of others, shall be investigated for legal liability by the relevant departments in accordance with the provisions of the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China and other relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 33 Whoever, in violation of Article 14 of this Law, fails to use core cryptography or ordinary cryptography as required, shall be ordered by the cryptography administrative department to make corrections or stop the illegal act, and be given a warning; if the circumstances are serious, the cryptography administrative department shall recommend that the relevant state organ or unit give sanctions or deal with the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons according to law.

Article 34 Where a case of leakage of core cryptography or ordinary cryptography occurs in violation of the provisions of this Law, the administrative department for secrecy and the cryptography administrative department shall recommend that the relevant state organ or unit give sanctions or deal with the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons according to law.
Where, in violation of paragraph 2 of Article 17 of this Law, upon discovering a leakage of core cryptography or ordinary cryptography or a major problem or risk that affects the security of core cryptography or ordinary cryptography, no immediate countermeasures are taken or a timely report is not made, the administrative department for secrecy and the cryptography administrative department shall recommend that the relevant state organ or unit give sanctions or deal with the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons according to law.

Article 35 Where a commercial cryptography testing and certification institution conducts commercial cryptography testing and certification in violation of paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 25 of this Law, the market supervision and administration department shall, jointly with the cryptography administrative department, order it to make corrections or stop the illegal act, give a warning, and confiscate the illegal gains; if the illegal gains are 300,000 RMB or more, a fine of not less than one time but not more than three times the illegal gains may be imposed concurrently; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 300,000 RMB, a fine of not less than 100,000 RMB but not more than 300,000 RMB may be imposed concurrently; if the circumstances are serious, the relevant qualifications shall be revoked according to law.

Article 36 Whoever, in violation of Article 26 of this Law, sells or provides commercial cryptography products that have not undergone testing and certification or have failed testing and certification, or provides commercial cryptography services that have not been certified or have failed certification, the market supervision and administration department shall, jointly with the cryptography administrative department, order it to make corrections or stop the illegal act, give a warning, and confiscate the illegal products and illegal gains; if the illegal gains are 100,000 RMB or more, a fine of not less than one time but not more than three times the illegal gains may be imposed concurrently; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 100,000 RMB, a fine of not less than 30,000 RMB but not more than 100,000 RMB may be imposed concurrently.

Article 37 Where an operator of critical information infrastructure, in violation of paragraph 1 of Article 27 of this Law, fails to use commercial cryptography as required, or fails to conduct commercial cryptography application security assessment as required, the cryptography administrative department shall order it to make corrections and give a warning; if it refuses to make corrections or causes consequences such as endangering network security, a fine of not less than 100,000 RMB but not more than 1,000,000 RMB shall be imposed, and a fine of not less than 10,000 RMB but not more than 100,000 RMB shall be imposed on the directly responsible person in charge.
Where an operator of critical information infrastructure, in violation of paragraph 2 of Article 27 of this Law, uses products or services that have not undergone security review or have failed security review, the relevant competent department shall order it to stop using them, and impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than ten times the procurement amount; a fine of not less than 10,000 RMB but not more than 100,000 RMB shall be imposed on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons.

Article 38 Whoever, in violation of the provisions of Article 28 on import licensing and export controls, imports or exports commercial cryptography, shall be punished according to law by the competent department of commerce under the State Council or the Customs.

Article 39 Whoever, in violation of Article 29 of this Law, engages in electronic certification services for e-government without recognition, the cryptography administrative department shall order it to make corrections or stop the illegal act, give a warning, and confiscate the illegal products and illegal gains; if the illegal gains are 300,000 RMB or more, a fine of not less than one time but not more than three times the illegal gains may be imposed concurrently; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 300,000 RMB, a fine of not less than 100,000 RMB but not more than 300,000 RMB may be imposed concurrently.

Article 40 Where staff members of the cryptography administrative department and relevant departments and units abuse their powers, neglect their duties, engage in malpractices for personal gain, or disclose or illegally provide to others the trade secrets and personal privacy that they know in the performance of their duties, they shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 41. Whoever violates this Law, if a crime is constituted, shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law; if damage is caused to others, the civil liability shall be borne according to law.
Article 42. The state cryptography administrative department shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, formulate cryptography management rules.

Article 43. The management measures for cryptography work of the Chinese People's Liberation Army and the Chinese People's Armed Police Force shall be formulated by the Central Military Commission in accordance with this Law.
Article 44. This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 2020.
